units.translation: 419. Ortygia: Phanodicus in his Deliaca (fr. 2 M. IV 473) has recorded the story about Ortygia. And Nicander in the first book of his Aetolica says that Delos was named from the Ortygia in Aetolia, writing as follows (fr. 5 Schn.): 'But they set out from Ortygia, daughter of Titan; some to Ephesus, some to the island formerly called Delos, others to the island bordering Sicily, ... whence all are called Ortygiae.' And so Delos is not, as the myth has it, from the transformation of Asteria,

the sister of Leto, but because all Ortygiae are colonies of the Ortygia in Aetolia.
421a. ἐπίβαθρα: embarkation fees, payment; but here the price for having now first embarked successfully on the ship.
b. προτεθείμεθα: instead of 'we do'; for 'to set' means 'to do'.

425. προχύτας: some say the barley grains, others the water which they are accustomed to pour into the ear of the sacrificial victim so that the victim nods assent. The preposition σύν is missing.

430a. χαλκείῳ πελέκει: Apollonius says in the first book of his Commentaries (M. IV 314) that iron was called 'bronze' by the ancients, not realizing that before iron was discovered they used bronze, as Hesiod also says (Op. 151): 'They worked with bronze, and there was no black iron.'

b. 〈τένοντας:〉 the sinews, from 'stretching'.

431a. περιρρηδὴς κερ〈άεσσιν〉: fallen headlong with force, dashed forward. Or [ἐπενεχθείς] instead of 'whirled around', as also in the poet (χ 84 sq.): 'and he fell headlong upon the table'. Antimachus uses the word for falling in a circle. But here it is instead of 'brought forward'.
